Ending on the final covered Saturday closes that week. events.event_name_es: Cine en el Parque: Pirates of the Caribbean
events.address: Old Mill Park, Mill Valley, CA 94941
events.description: Free outdoor screening of Pirates of the Caribbean at Old Mill Park, part of the City of Mill Valley's Movies in the Park series. Starts at dusk, around 7 pm. Bring blankets, low lawn chairs and a picnic.

events.internal_notes:
Aug 11 (Finding Nemo, id 588) is the only screening at the Community Center rather than Old Mill Park. Sourced 2026-07-29 from Alexandra directly, corroborated by web search (Jun 2-Oct 13 season, dusk ~7 PM, Aug 11 at the Community Center Lawn). NOTE: the city's deep link cityofmillvalley.gov/840/Movies-in-the-Park currently returns 404, so the generic Recreation page is used instead - re-check the deep link next sweep.
RETIRED 2026-10-13-dated record, set Inactive 2026-09-08. This is the 2023 season's FINALE, misdated. A Mill Valley Chamber write-up describes Pirates of the Caribbean as the final movie of the Jun 2 - Oct 13 season, screening "this Friday the 13th" - Oct 13 is a Friday in 2023, a Tuesday in 2026. Nothing published anywhere confirms a screening on 2026-10-13.
Inactive rather than deleted, per the standing preference: the record keeps its provenance and can be reactivated with a corrected date if Mill Valley Recreation confirms a real 2026 or 2027 season. Its sibling id 788 was cancelled the same day on Alexandra's word, which is independent confirmation that this series is not running as stored.
SOURCE AUDITED 2026-09-08, and the season was three years stale.
The stored note read "2026 season runs Jun 2 - Oct 13 on 2nd Tuesdays". The city's OWN calendar entry for that opener (cityofmillvalley.gov/Calendar.aspx?EID=2316) reads "Friday, June 2, 2023 - The Nightmare Before Christmas". Jun 2 and Oct 13 are Fridays in 2023; in 2026 they fall on Tuesdays, which is where the invented "2nd Tuesdays" rule came from - the dates were kept from the wrong year and a weekday rule was reverse-engineered to fit them.
ROOT SOURCE: ronniesawesomelist.com/outdoor-movies, sweep source 11. That page is an article published 27 June 2017, still live and still reading as current, listing Jul 7 / Aug 4 / Sep 8 / Oct 6 at Old Mill Park - all 2017 Fridays. CLAUDE.md already records that this record's predecessor carried exactly those four dates. The same page has now produced bad data twice.
WHY IT SURVIVED: cityofmillvalley.gov/840/Movies-in-the-Park 404s, and still did on 2026-09-08. On 2026-07-29 the same pass corrected id 310 (Concerts on the Plaza), which had inherited a stale date from the same list, because the city publishes a working page for it (833). There was nothing to check the movies against, and the 404 was recorded as a footnote rather than treated as a reason to distrust the data.
THE REAL PATTERN IS FRIDAYS: the Mill Valley Chamber lists 2025 as Fri Aug 1 (Luca), Fri Sep 5 (Inside Out 2), Fri Oct 3 (Little Mermaid). No 2026 season is published anywhere findable. Re-source by phone - Mill Valley Recreation, 415-383-1370 - before re-adding.

events.description_es: Música, movimiento y cuentos con Ingrid: canciones, baile y sorpresas para bebés, niños pequeños y sus cuidadores, en la biblioteca de Corte Madera.
events.internal_notes:
Converted from recurring id 41 on 2026-09-03, THE SAME DAY I set that record's rule - and the rule was wrong. Earlier today it was reactivated as Monthly '2nd and 4th Thursdays', derived from the only two dates then visible, Oct 8 and Oct 22. Reading the MCFL feed out to December shows five: Oct 8, Oct 22, Nov 5, Nov 19, Dec 3 = the 2nd, 4th, 1st, 3rd and 1st Thursday. That is every FOURTEEN DAYS, not an ordinal.
THE LESSON IS NOT 'CHECK HARDER'. A fortnightly series impersonates an ordinal rule in any month where the two happen to coincide, which October did. No number of dates inside ONE month can tell them apart - you need dates that straddle a month boundary. Open item 44 said this record's cadence could not be derived from a single instance; two was not enough either.
The rule would have been right through October and wrong from Nov 5: it generated Nov 12 and Nov 26 against real sessions on Nov 5 and Nov 19, so a family would have arrived on the wrong Thursday twice and missed both real ones, then Dec 10 and Dec 24 against a real Dec 3.
TWO FURTHER PUBLIC ERRORS were found in the record while converting it, neither introduced today and neither previously noticed. `description` still read 'Held on the 2nd, 4th, and 5th Wednesdays of each month' - wrong ordinal AND wrong weekday. `description_es` read 'el 2do, 4to y 5to miércoles de cada mes en South Novato' - wrong ordinal, wrong weekday, and THE WRONG BRANCH. The venue field had been corrected from South Novato to Corte Madera at some point, but the Spanish description was left behind, so Spanish-speaking families were being sent to a different library in a different town. Both descriptions rewritten, and neither now states a schedule in prose - the dates are the record.
DELETED rather than retired, same reasoning as id 720 earlier today: a retired record still lands on computed dates and leaves permanent COLLISION findings (open item 45).
Dates from the MCFL bibliocommons feed read to 2026-12-31; re-check when December runs out.

events.event_name: Dolly Parton's Imagination Library — Free Books by Mail
events.event_name_es: Imagination Library de Dolly Parton — Libros Gratis por Correo
events.address: Books are mailed to your home — there is nowhere to go
events.notes: First of each month. A standing programme rather than a dated event — register once and a book arrives every month until your child turns five. There is nothing to attend and nothing to return.
events.description:
A free, high-quality book mailed to your child every month, from birth until their fifth birthday, personalised with your child's name. Marin County Free Library runs the programme locally with First 5 Marin, and all Marin County families qualify.

HOW TO SIGN UP: go to marinlibrary.org/imagination-library and click Register Online. You will need your child's name and date of birth and your mailing address. When you enrol you can choose bilingual English and Spanish books — California is the only state in the country that offers them.

The first book arrives about 8 to 12 weeks after your registration is approved, and a new one roughly every 30 days after that. It is completely free, no library card is needed, and there is nothing to return. Questions about enrolling: daphne@first5marin.org.
events.description_es:
Un libro gratuito y de calidad enviado por correo a tu hijo o hija cada mes, desde el nacimiento hasta que cumple cinco años, personalizado con su nombre. La Biblioteca Pública del Condado de Marin dirige el programa localmente junto con First 5 Marin, y todas las familias del condado de Marin pueden participar.

CÓMO INSCRIBIRSE: entra en marinlibrary.org/imagination-library y haz clic en Register Online. Necesitarás el nombre y la fecha de nacimiento de tu hijo o hija y tu dirección postal. Al inscribirte puedes elegir libros bilingües en inglés y español: California es el único estado del país que los ofrece.

El primer libro llega entre 8 y 12 semanas después de que se apruebe la inscripción, y después llega uno nuevo aproximadamente cada 30 días. Es totalmente gratuito, no se necesita tarjeta de biblioteca y no hay que devolver nada. Para preguntas sobre la inscripción: daphne@first5marin.org.
events.internal_notes:
Added 2026-09-03 at Alexandra's request: 'On the carousel, add Dolly Parton's imagination library as the first event. When you click into the card provide a description of how to sign up through the Marin Library system, and the link.'
THIS IS THE FIRST RECORD TO USE `pinned: true`, a new flag added to selectFeatured() in the same commit. It is needed because this is NOT an event: there is no date, no venue and nothing to attend, so occ() would never find an occurrence and elig() would reject it for not being One-off. The pin makes it eligible regardless of cadence, always count as occurring, and sit at the FRONT of reserved[] - which is emptied into the strip before the scored loop runs, so position in reserved is display order.
USE THE PIN SPARINGLY. It costs one of the strip's nine slots every single day, permanently. Two pins would cost two.
`cadence: Monthly` with a first-of-month ordinal is deliberate: the pin governs the carousel, but the record also lands in the ordinary feed, and once a month is a light touch for a standing programme. Without an ordinal a Monthly record renders NOWHERE (rule 9), so the phrase in notes is load-bearing.
`venue` and `address` say plainly that books are mailed, so nobody turns up somewhere. Alexandra also flagged this as a good candidate for the Resources page - not done here, and worth doing as well rather than instead, since the carousel slot is time-limited attention and Resources is where people look when they want it.
UPDATED 2026-09-05 on Alexandra's instruction: remove the September 5 date, keep it a standing carousel item, and point the website at marinlibrary.org/imagination-library/.
THE DATE WAS A RENDERING BUG, NOT A FIELD. Nothing on this record ever said Sep 5. occ() hands every pinned card TODAY's date so it always counts as occurring, and renderFeatured() printed that date verbatim - so the card read 'Sep 5' as though it were a one-day event, and would have read 'Sep 6' tomorrow. Editing this record could not have fixed it; the fix is a featMeta() helper in index.html that renders 'Sign up any time' for pinned cards and omits the town.
Town changed from 'Marin County (mailed to your home)' to 'Marin County' and venue to 'Mailed to your home', so the detail line reads 'Mailed to your home - Marin County' instead of repeating itself. location_group stays San Rafael: rule 8 forbids a county-level location_group and the town filter still has to place this somewhere.
Sign-up steps rewritten from marinlibrary.org/imagination-library/ rather than the national site. That is what she asked for and it is also more accurate for Marin: run locally with First 5 Marin, all Marin families qualify, books personalised with the child's name, first book in 8-12 weeks (NOT the 8-10 I had written from the national page), and California is the only state offering the bilingual option. Enrolment contact: daphne@first5marin.org.
RULE 9 REGRESSION, CAUGHT BY THE LINT AND FIXED THE SAME MINUTE (2026-09-05). Rewriting notes for the 'standing event' change dropped the ordinal phrase, so this Monthly record had NO occurrence rule and would have rendered NOWHERE in the feed - the exact silent-vanish failure rule 9 describes. --notes-lint reported it as STRANDED, because internal_notes still explained an ordinal that notes no longer carried. 'First of each month.' restored to the front of notes. The pin governs the carousel independently, so this only ever affected the feed.
OPEN QUESTION for Alexandra: it now appears in the ordinary feed once a month as well as permanently on the carousel. If she wants it carousel-ONLY there is no clean field for that - the nearest lever is status Inactive, which shouldShowEvent() hides from the feed while selectFeatured() ignores status entirely, but that is a side effect rather than a designed behaviour and would break if a status check were ever added to the strip. Ask before using it.
